title: Beta Film Takes ‘Rex – Vienna Calling’ Worldwide as Season 2 Goes Into Production (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Beta Film has unveiled a broad international sales footprint for “Rex – Vienna Calling,” the latest incarnation of the three-decade-old “Rex – A Cop
body:
Beta Film has unveiled a broad international sales footprint for “Rex – Vienna Calling,” the latest incarnation of the three-decade-old “Rex – A Cop’s Best Friend” franchise, as production gets underway on a second season.

	The series has been sold to SBS in Australia, Rai in Italy and TV 2 in Denmark. Elsewhere in Europe, buyers include Alpha TV in Greece, HRT in Croatia, Planet TV in Slovenia, STVR in Slovakia, Nova in Bulgaria and TVR in Romania, while Baltic deals take in Duo Media Networks in Estonia, SIA Tet in Latvia and LNK in Lithuania.
	

	Action Channel in Japan and SHANT TV in Armenia are also on board, with further sales under negotiation.


	The deals come as the evergreen IP continues to find traction in an increasingly on-demand television market. Audience analytics firm PlumResearch describes mature streaming markets as shifting “from hits to habits,” with much viewing taking place across the long tail rather than being concentrated solely around new releases.

	The longevity of “Rex” offers a case in point. Over its 30-year history, the police-dog franchise has spawned multiple local adaptations. Canadian remake “Hudson & Rex,” another long-running Beta title, was recently renewed for a tenth season.

	“Rex – Vienna Calling” stars Maximilian Brückner (“War Horse,” “Cherry Blossoms”) as detective Max Steiner, who teams with German Shepherd Rex to tackle cases across Vienna. Six new feature-length episodes are currently shooting at some of the Austrian capital’s most recognizable locations.

	The first season opened to almost 1.6 million viewers on Germany’s SAT.1, posting a 7% overall share and 9.9% among 14-49s. In Austria, the six feature-length episodes averaged 701,000 viewers and a 27% share on ORF, while the Italian premiere on Rai 2 drew more than 750,000 viewers and a 5.6% share, rising above one million once on-demand and catch-up viewing was included.
	

	Produced by MR Film in co-production with SAT.1 and ORF, “Rex – Vienna Calling” is distributed worldwide by Beta Film. The series is backed by FISAplus, the Austrian Television Fund and the state of Lower Austria.

schema.headline: Beta Film Takes ‘Rex – Vienna Calling’ Worldwide as Season 2 Goes Into Production (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Mubi Takes Global on Los Javis ‘La Mesías’ and Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s ‘Riot Police’ as Movistar Plus Rolls Out Iconic Hits Around the World (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Mubi has taken worldwide rights to two iconic series from Movistar Plus International, the overseas distributor of the biggest Spanish pay TV and SV
body:
Mubi has taken worldwide rights to two iconic series from Movistar Plus International, the overseas distributor of the biggest Spanish pay TV and SVOD operator: “La Mesias,” from “La Bola Negra” directors Los Javis, and “Riot Police,” the first premium TV series from “The Beloved” director Rodrigo Sorogoyen.

	Further headlines: Nominated on Sept. 23 for an International Emmy, four-part “The Anatomy of a Moment,” from Alberto Rodriguez (“The Tigers”), has rolled out in further territories in Europe.
	

	The in-all 33 new deals were unveiled during the first day of trading at Madrid’s mega-market and forum Iberseries & Platino Industria, where Movistar Plus has a large market presence led by screenings or presentations of top titles bound for October’s Mipcom.


	On Tuesday, Movistar Plus International hosted a showcase, screening and cocktail of Spain’s sex trade chronicle “El Castillo,” a standout at San Sebastián; a screening of withering LOL Millennial comedy “Many People Have to Die,” marking out creator Victoria Martín as a major Spanish comedic talent; and a presentation of “Killing a Bear,” based crime drama turning on the deep social conflict surrounding the death of brown bear Cachou, found dead in a ravine in the Pyrenees in 2020. The “small, local story vividly illustrated the polarized world we live in,” creators Jorge and Alberto Sánchez Cabezudo have told Variety.

	‘La Mesías’

	A Movistar Plus Original, large scale “La Mesías” delivered a first instance of Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s full-on creativity, working with the budget they required, shooting each episode with different genre influences – psychodrama, sci-fi, procedural and musical – and a pop sensibility and varying formats across multiple timelines, all of which they have now repeated in “La Bola Negra.”
	

	“La Mesías,” like La Bola Negra,” also explores legacy and repression, here the psychological trauma left by a messianic mother, who turns her family into a cult.

	“The series talks about religion, but as a form of education and this is what makes it interesting,” told Variety on set in 2023.

	Key territories for the Mubi deal were announced in exclusivity by Variety in July.

	‘Riot Police’

	World premiering at San Sebastián in 2020 and starring “The Beloved’s” Victoria Luengo, Riot Police confirmed Sorogoyen’s ability to bring a big screen punch to his first premium series.

	A six part series “Riot Police” also underscored his ability to mix genre and social point, exploring the failures and fragility of the masculine psyche as a riot police squad become the subject of an internal police enquiry led by Luengo’s character after bungling an eviction. The series closed early deals with HBO Latin America and Canal+ in France.

	“The series I’ve seen rarely evolve in style,”Soroyogen told Variety in 2020. But Riot Police does in the use of hand-held, anamorphic fisheye lense camerawork for the eviction moving to a 15 minutes sequence shot in final episode.

	‘The Anatomy of a Moment’

	Co-produced with Arte France, starring “Money Heist’s” Alvaro Morte, “The Anatomy of a Moment” delivers Rodríguez’s fictionalized vision of how three key figures of “Shakespearian stature,” Rodríguez has said– Spanish Prime Minister Adolfo Suárez, Spanish Communist Party head Santiago Carrillo and armed forces chief Manuel Gutiérrez Mellado – wrestled democracy for Spain over 1976-77and almost lost it in a 1981 botched coup d’état. New international distribution takes in pubcasters RTP (Portugal), RTS (Switzerland), RTV (Slovenia) and Cinob0 (Greece).

	More Top Sellers: ‘Querer,’ ‘The New Years,’ ‘The Nameless’

	A top best series Grand Prix winner at Series Mania last year, Alauda Ruiz de Azua’s’s marital rape series Querer,” part family drama, part courtroom thriller, she has observed, continues to roll out around the world. Already acquired by Arte, Querer has now been licensed to Cinobo Poland, Italy’s MyMoviesOne, Latvia’s Latvia’s Mobilais and South Korea’s LG Plus.
	

	Movistar Plus International has closed Greece and Poland, both with Cinobo, and Latvia (Latvijas Mobilais) on Sorogoyen’s “The New Years,” on-off couple romantic saga that played Venice in 2024 alongside Alfonso Cuarón’s Cate Blanchett starrer “Disclaimer” for Apple TV+, and Thomas Vinterberg’s big StudioCanal play “Families Like Ours.

	France’s Filmo, Media4Fun and South Korea’s LG Plus have bought “The Nameless,” a portrait of evil family horror series from Filmax (“[REC]”), Pau Freixas (“The Red Band Society,” “You Shall Not Lie”) and Pol Cortecans (“You Shall Not Lie”),

	A Drill-Down on More Deals:

	*Cinobo Greece has picked up two seasons of “Bellas Artes” plus “A 100-Million Reward.”

	*Filmo has also licensed “La vida breve.”

	*Flow, the big Argentine streaming service covering Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay, has become one of the first operators to buy “Many People Have to Die,” as well as “The Center,” “La Caza. Irati” and doc “Bisbal.”

	*”Riot Police” also sold to Media4Fun.

	*Italy’s MyMovieOne has acquired global electricity power outage anthology “OffWorld,” including episodes by Sorogoyen, Rodríguez, Isaki la Cuesta, Isa Campo and Rail Arévalo.

	*Poland’s TVP has taken “La Canción,” from “Hierro” and “Rapa” creators Pepe Coira and Fran Araujo, placing Spain’s stunning 1968 Eurovision win in Spain’s dawn-of-democracy later liberty. Further acquisitions take in Costa del Sol mob lawyer comedy “Marbella,” crime investigation thriller “La Caza.Irati,” from Banijay’s DLO Producciones and two seasons of Canary Islands-set murder mystery “Hierro.”

	*South Korea’s LG, a streaming service, has licensed “El centro,” “La Caza. Irati,” two ‘Hierro’ seasons, “El dentista’,” and “La vida breve.”

title: Greta Thunberg Makes Surprise Appearance at Zurich Premiere of ‘My Home of Wind and Sand,’ Denounces Occupation of Western Sahara
description: Greta Thunberg made a surprise appearance on Tuesday at Zurich Film Festival, where she joined the screening of a new documentary “My Home of Wind a
body:
Greta Thunberg made a surprise appearance on Tuesday at Zurich Film Festival, where she joined the screening of a new documentary “My Home of Wind and Sand,” which looks at the occupation of Western Sahara by Morocco.

	Calling the film “powerful” and able to “create change,” Thunberg minced no words when speaking about the world’s attitude toward the region. “There’s this extreme hypocrisy that makes me so, so angry and upset,” she said. 
	

	“For me, this movie was so much about betrayal. There are so many levels of betrayal. First, there’s the occupation and the violence itself that somehow becomes ‘normal’ or is viewed as normal. It’s not easy to get any media attention and clicks, which is another betrayal,” she said. Then there’s “the betrayal of the international solidarity movement.” 


	Western Sahara has been occupied by Morocco since 1975. It is often referred to as the last colonial conflict in Africa. In 2025, the U.S. reaffirmed its recognition of Moroccan sovereignty.

	Recently, Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” faced backlash for filming scenes in the Western Sahara, with Nolan accused of “contributing to Morocco’s repression of the Sahrawi people.” The Western Sahara International Film Festival (FiSahara) even put out a statement urging him to stop production.

	Turning to the film’s protagonist, Sahrawi human rights activist Najla Mohamed-Lamin, Thunberg said: “I’m convinced that people like you do not want thanks or applause, but action. It falls on every single one of us in this room, especially us privileged people who have a platform and access to resources, to take that moral obligation to amplify the Western Sahara struggles.”
	

	“Otherwise, we are nothing more than hypocrites,” she added.

	Mohamed-Lamin, whose life and fight for Western Sahara independence is depicted in the doc, became emotional, noting: “As I was watching these 10 years of my life, I couldn’t stop thinking about all the stories and lives in the last 50 years that nobody has heard of, which are probably far more inspiring than mine: My grandmother, my sister who passed away, my mother, all our neighbors. All the thousands of people we buried in these camps who would have never wished to be buried there.”

	Mohamed-Lamin added, “As somebody who’s a refugee forgotten in the desert, you’re always looking for a little window to share your story. I didn’t know it would develop into a documentary. The only thing I know is that I carry the message of my people, and I will share it everywhere I go: In a documentary, in an article, in a train station or on a plane, because I’m the voice. The world has to know the truth.”

	Directed by Patrick Wally, the film is sold by Lightdox.

	Thunberg, who visited a Sahrawi refugee camp in 2025, also took part in a special panel discussion on “Resistance and Activism for Western Sahara.”

schema.headline: Greta Thunberg Makes Surprise Appearance at Zurich Premiere of ‘My Home of Wind and Sand,’ Denounces Occupation of Western Sahara

title: Producer-Led The Creatives Enters Jointly Owned Holding Structure as Anton Studios Joins as Partner and Minority Investor (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Fast-growing European studio Anton Studios is taking a minority position as a partner and investor in The Creatives. The group, first founded as a l
body:
Fast-growing European studio Anton Studios is taking a minority position as a partner and investor in The Creatives. The group, first founded as a long-term strategic partnership in 2021, is moving into a solidified company, with a jointly owned holding structure. The new model will see The Creatives become the first European-rooted producer-owned group of its scale in film and television, with Romain Bessi remaining as CEO.

	The Creatives consists of some of the leading production companies in Europe, as well as one each in Israel and the U.S. They are Haut et Court and Unité in France, Komplizen and Razor Film in Germany, the U.K.’s Good Chaos, Lemming Film in Netherlands and Belgium, Maipo Film in Norway, Spiro in Israel and the U.S.’s Masha.
	

	Led by Sébastien Raybaud, Anton’s projects include “In Love,” starring George Clooney and Annette Bening; “Pumping Black,” starring Jonathan Bailey and Natalie Portman; and the crime thriller “My Darling California,” featuring Jessica Chastain, Chris Evan, Chris Pine, Mikey Madison and Don Cheadle.


	Anton’s investment in The Creatives reinforces the financial strength of the group and provides additional access to equity financing. The Creatives will be formally created at closing, following technical steps expected to take a few months.

	Bessi brings three decades of experience in production, distribution and broadcasting, having built two international studios in Newen Studios/Studio TF1, which he led as chairman and CEO within the TF1 Group until 2024, and Studiocanal, where he served as group COO. Prior to this, he served as CFO for the Canal+ channels in France and CEO for Canal+ in the Nordics.
	

	Speaking with Variety, Bessi said this consolidated company was “always the point.”

	“Five years ago, all of these producers decided that, because they didn’t want anyone to buy them out and they wanted to share their expertise and contacts, they would create a form of club, where they would informally meet every month and co-produce together,” he added. “They have now been doing this very successfully for years, and they decided that, because it was working so well, they would become a group.”

	“But they didn’t know how to do it, which is when they reached out to me,” he said. “Of course, creating a group costs money, so during the last year and a half I was structuring the group and looking for an investor to bring some money into the holding company.”

	Bessi said it took over a year to find Anton. The Creatives had several other offers, but they had a number of strict demands for whoever would come in as a financial partner. “We wanted a European investor, not only because of the perception, but also because of regulation. They had to be European; they had to be someone who understands the industry—meaning that you can have good years and bad years, and you need to take some risk. That was very important.”

	Finding the investor was “not so easy,” because the model built by The Creatives is “very new in the industry.” All 17 producers in the group are shareholders and control the group. “It’s very unique. Usually, you have one person or company who gets the shares and the control. Because of that, some investors were a bit concerned about the governance of the group,” Bessi said.

	“We wanted someone who would agree to take a minority stake and would not require distribution or sales,” he added. “Then, of course, there was a valuation, which was important for the producers, and we wanted someone who would respect that valuation. Lastly, we needed someone we knew, and I knew Anton very well because it was created 15 years ago, to implement a state financing deal for Studiocanal. At that time, I was the CEO.”

	In the end, the producers decided in favor of Anton. Now, all agreements are signed, and The Creatives are “ready to go.”

	By “ready to go,” Bessi means realizing the group’s vision of becoming the leading “one-stop-shop” production company in Europe for major distributors and streamers. The exec sees The Creatives as the place where these companies can have access to “elevated content and festival movies and series.”
	

	“When they come to us, they suddenly have access to many talents, many projects out of many European countries,” he said. “It offers a wide diversity of very good foreign content. We have the scale of the group now. It’s strong enough and financially reliable, so it can be a very interesting one-stop shop for major companies instead of them going country by country to work with these leading producers.”

	“Our goal is to accelerate and enhance the model so we can allow the producers to develop the project they want to develop, be ready, take more risks, gather the best talent and use each other’s connections,” he emphasized. “We want these people to do what they do best: to produce and attract talent.”

	Work produced by The Creatives has drawn over 140 awards at major festivals and awards ceremonies worldwide, including a Cannes Palme d’Or and a Venice Grand Jury Prize, alongside multiple Academy Award nominations and wins. 

	Signature lead-produced titles include Komplizen’s Oscar-nominated “Toni Erdmann”; Haut et Court’s Palme d’Or winner “The Class”; Good Chaos’ “Sisu” films, which both topped global streaming charts; Spiro’s Venice Grand Jury Prize winner “Foxtrot”; Razor Film’s Oscar-nominated “Waltz With Bashir”; Maipo Film’s Canneseries winner “A Better Man”; Unité’s multi-César winner “Souleymane’s Story”; Masha’s hit series “False Flag”; and Lemming Film’s six-time Dutch Academy Award winner “Sweet Dreams.”

title: Fiona Lowe, Daughter of Chad Lowe and Kim Painter, Dies at 13
description:
Fiona Hepler Lowe, the daughter of actor Chad Lowe and Kim Painter, has died. She was 13.

	Fiona’s death was confirmed to People on Tuesday by the
body:
Fiona Hepler Lowe, the daughter of actor Chad Lowe and Kim Painter, has died. She was 13.

	Fiona’s death was confirmed to People on Tuesday by the Lowe family, who wrote “We are deeply heartbroken by the loss of our beloved Fiona” in a statement. Fiona was described by her family as “a loving young girl who was smart, creative, and loved to dance.” “She was adored by her sisters and she was deeply loved by her parents,” they wrote. “In fact, she was the light of our lives.”
	

	“Her passing is devastating for our entire family, and we ask for prayers and privacy at this time. If you or someone you know is struggling with mental health, please reach out to the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline by calling or texting 988,” the statement concluded.


	Fiona was born on Nov. 16, 2012, to Chad and Kim, and was the second daughter in the family. Mabel Painter, 17, was born in 2009, and Nixie Barbara, 10, was born in 2016. Her middle name, Hepler, was Lowe’s late mother’s maiden name and is his brother Rob Lowe’s middle name, per People. Lowe and Painter got married in 2019.

	Chad has appeared on shows including “Pretty Little Liars” and “Supergirl,” among others. He won an Emmy for playing Jesse McKenna on “Life Goes On.” Rob is best known for roles across film and television, including “The Outsiders,” “St. Elmo’s Fire,” “Parks and Recreation” and more. 

	Fiona is survived by her father, Chad, her mother, Kim and her sisters, Mabel and Nixie.

	If you or anyone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please call the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline by dialing 988 or go to SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

schema.headline: Fiona Lowe, Daughter of Chad Lowe and Kim Painter, Dies at 13

title: Aaron Sorkin Says ‘Social Reckoning’ Reshoots Had Nothing to Do With Trailer Backlash, Explains Why Trump Isn’t Named: It’s ‘Not a Red-Blue Thing’
description: Ahead of the release of “The Social Reckoning” on Oct. 9, director Aaron Sorkin is telling all on the film’s much-discussed reshoots, limited test s
body:
Ahead of the release of “The Social Reckoning” on Oct. 9, director Aaron Sorkin is telling all on the film’s much-discussed reshoots, limited test screenings and why Trump is never named explicitly, despite the January 6 riot playing a part in the plot.

	In a recent interview with Vanity Fair, Sorkin explained that the reshoots, which took place after the trailer was released, had nothing to do with the initial mixed reactions and were simply to “make it better.” “We weren’t correcting anything,” he said. “There are two kinds of reshoots: one is the ‘Oh, we’re in trouble. We need to reshoot this.’ And that usually happens on $150 million superhero movies. The other kinds of reshoots are ‘Oh, we really like this movie. It’s good. Let’s make it better.’”
	

	He explained that Sony Pictures chairman and CEO Tom Rothman asked if there was anything he’d want to reshoot, if given the option. “Yeah, I would go back and rewrite and reshoot the whole thing,” said Sorkin, before clarifying that there were only two scenes he felt he could add something to. “And so he opened the checkbook and gave us three days of shooting.”


	A follow-up to 2010’s “The Social Network,” “The Social Reckoning” follows former Facebook engineer and whistleblower Frances Haugen (Mikey Madison) and Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz ( Jeremy Allen White) as they expose the inner workings of Facebook. Their work culminated in “The Facebook Files,” a 2021 investigative series revealing Facebook’s harmful effects on teens and its role in spreading misinformation, including content linked to political violence. 
	

	However, despite the relevance of politics to the real-life events the film is based on and its recreation of Jan. 6, Trump is not mentioned by name in “The Social Reckoning,” a decision Sorkin stands by.

	“I want to be clear: I was never asked to do that, to not mention Trump by name,” he said. “I turned in the script and a day or two later met with Tom Rothman, who was full speed ahead on it. And I promised him, unprovoked, that we would not see any Trump signage, no ‘Make America Great Again.’ The movie is about Facebook’s role and the rise of divisiveness, extremism, and hyper-partisanship in the country. It is not a red-blue thing, even though, obviously, it will be felt that way.”

	Sorkin also revealed that a scene in which one of Facebook’s senior officials says, “I don’t know what that bitch thinks she’s doing,” had to be rewritten to remove the expletive, per the outside legal firm hired by Sony’s. “The lawyer said, ‘Unless you can show me that at one point a senior Facebook executive referred to an ex-employee as a bitch, you can’t do that.’ So it was that.” 

	On the subject of test screenings, Sorkin said that the studio “had a real concern for secrecy,” which meant the test screenings were each “70 people on the studio lot, all of them Sony employees.” “It is not a great polling sample,” he added.

schema.headline: Aaron Sorkin Says ‘Social Reckoning’ Reshoots Had Nothing to Do With Trailer Backlash, Explains Why Trump Isn’t Named: It’s ‘Not a Red-Blue Thing’

title: Zygi Kamasa’s U.K. Film Distributor True Brit Entertainment Files for Administration Due to ‘Extremely Challenging Market Conditions’
description: True Brit Entertainment, the U.K. theatrical distributor that launched less than three years ago, has filed for administration, a British legal proc
body:
True Brit Entertainment, the U.K. theatrical distributor that launched less than three years ago, has filed for administration, a British legal process similar to Chapter 11 bankruptcy. 

	The company, which was founded by former Lionsgate U.K. & Europe CEO and Marv Studios Group CEO Zygi Kamasa, becomes the latest casualty of the U.K.’s extremely tough distribution market, having failed to ignite the local box office despite critically-acclaimed releases including “The Death of Robin Hood” starring Hugh Jackman. 
	

	“In extremely challenging market conditions, the company has taken the difficult decision to enter administration.” Kamasa said in a statement sent to Variety. “An independent specialist has now been appointed to oversee the company and assess the options available, with the aim of achieving the best possible outcome for the company and its creditors.”


	True Brit was announced in Nov 2023 with a focus exclusively on U.K. films for theatrical release, launching with a stated aim to invest in and release 4-8 titles a year and co-finance over $50million worth of productions annually. The new venture came with funding led by talent management and entertainment company Three Six Zero, which reps names including Calvin Harris, Frank Ocean, FKA Twigs, plus a minority investment from Matthew Vaughn’s Marv. 

	The first True Brit release was “The Critic” starring Ian McKellen and Gemma Arterton, which it acquired out of Toronto in 2023 and put in U.K. cinemas the following year. This was followed by the Danny Dyer comedy “Marching Powder,” which hit a high note, grossing more than $4 million in the U.K. and Ireland. But subsequent releases, including Gurinder Chadha’s musical comedy-drama “Christmas Karma” and the boxing drama “Giant,” both of which True Brit co-produced, struggled, as did “The Death of Robin Hood,” which earned under $800,000. 
	

	The latest release, the Bella Ramsey-starring coming-of-age comedy-drama “Sunny Dancer,” despite an impressive promotional campaign and buzz from its world premiere in Berlin, also failed to land, underlining the ongoing struggles in the U.K. for independent film. 

	Upcoming titles for True Brit include Anthony Wonke’s boxing biopic “In the Shadows,” which is due to world premiere later this month at the BFI London Film Festival, and the Maika Monroe-led psychological horror comedy “Victorian Psycho,” which premiered in Cannes. It’s unknown what will now happen to these releases.

	Variety‘s sister publication Deadline was first to report the news of True Brit going into administration.

schema.headline: Zygi Kamasa’s U.K. Film Distributor True Brit Entertainment Files for Administration Due to ‘Extremely Challenging Market Conditions’

title: Karan Johar to End ‘Koffee With Karan’ After 22 Years With Final Season on JioHotstar: ‘The Decision Is Emotional and Personal’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Indian media personality Karan Johar will end “Koffee With Karan” after 22 years. 

	His celebrity chat show returns for a ninth and final season, s
body:
Indian media personality Karan Johar will end “Koffee With Karan” after 22 years. 

	His celebrity chat show returns for a ninth and final season, streaming on JioHotstar from Oct. 14.

	Since its 2004 debut, the show has run eight seasons and 161 episodes. On its couch, top Indian stars have talked about friendships, romances, breakups and marriages. Many of those conversations went viral or became news in their own right.


	“‘Koffee With Karan’ has been such a large part of my identity in the entertainment industry… I still can’t believe it’s been 22 years and now this will be my ninth season,” Johar said.
	

	Johar said hosting the show had been deeply rewarding, but that he had come to the realization that “I want to spend the next decade of my life directing more movies… telling many more stories… so with a heavy heart I am making this season my last.”

	“Koffee With Karan” premiered on Star World on 2004, with Shah Rukh Khan and Kajol as its first guests. The first season also brought Amitabh Bachchan on with his son Abhishek Bachchan, and paired Aishwarya Rai with Sanjay Leela Bhansali. The show ran for six seasons on Star World through 2019, and its second season was also simulcast on Star One in 2007. By its sixth season, episodes also streamed on Hotstar, which, like the channel, was owned by Star India. Kareena Kapoor and Kajol are among its most frequent guests.

	In January 2019, a Season 6 episode with cricketers Hardik Pandya and K.L. Rahul caused an uproar over Pandya’s remarks about women. Hotstar took the episode down from its service. The Board of Control for Cricket in India issued show-cause notices to both players and briefly suspended them from the national team.
	

	In 2022, Johar posted a statement suggesting the show was over. Hours later he revealed that it was leaving television, not ending, and would move to Disney+ Hotstar as a streaming exclusive. Johar’s Dharmatic Entertainment took over production from SOL India for Season 7, which launched that July. Season 8 opened in October 2023 with Ranveer Singh and Deepika Padukone. In February 2025, Disney+ Hotstar merged with JioCinema to form JioHotstar.

	“This will be the last time I will be on a couch that has been synonymous with conversations, candor and well… controversies… the decision is emotional and personal to me… But I am hoping the legacy of love the show has given me continues to brew in people’s hearts,” Johar said.

	“‘Koffee With Karan’ is the talk show that brought the biggest celebrities into viewers’ living rooms and built a fandom that very few shows have matched. For over two decades, it has given audiences an intimate, irreverent and often unexpected glimpse into the lives of the people they love watching, becoming a part of pop culture phenomenon,” added Alok Jain, Hindi and English entertainment business (streaming, TV and studios), JioStar. “As Karan raises the coffee mug one last time, we celebrate the extraordinary legacy of a show that has consistently delivered great content and created a lasting connection with audiences. At JioHotstar, we remain committed to bringing audiences the very best in entertainment, and we are delighted to bring this final chapter of ‘Koffee With Karan’ to them.”

	Johar heads Dharma Productions. His directing credits include “Kuch Kuch Hota Hai,” “Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham” and “Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani.”

schema.headline: Karan Johar to End ‘Koffee With Karan’ After 22 Years With Final Season on JioHotstar: ‘The Decision Is Emotional and Personal’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Amazon MGM Execs Javiera Balmaceda, Nicole Morganti Talk Big Spanish-Language Action Swings, the Push for Scale at Iberseries & Platino Industria
description: Speaking at the Iberseries & Platino Industria conference in Madrid, Amazon MGM execs Javiera Balmaceda and Nicole Morganti offered a candid look at
body:
Speaking at the Iberseries & Platino Industria conference in Madrid, Amazon MGM execs Javiera Balmaceda and Nicole Morganti offered a candid look at how the streamer decides which non-English language projects to back, pointing to “Zeta” in Spain and “Venganza” in Mexico as examples of taking bigger swings in genre.

	The two executives said Amazon’s international teams are in frequent creative contact, sharing scripts, casting ideas and talent. “We share talent globally — actors, creators, writers and authors,” said Morganti, Prime Video head of international originals, Italy & Southern Europe.
	

	The real work, however, comes when a project needs to be sold internally.


	Morganti said “Zeta,” an espionage actioner starring Mario Casas and produced by Pablo Isla’s Fonte Films,  was a chance to prove that Spain could deliver a big action movie with a distinctly Spanish identity. “Spain has a strong ability to make action,” she said, noting that the film also benefited from its mix of action, family and emotion. The movie ranked among Amazon Prime Video most watched Global Top Ten hits earlier this year. 

	Balmaceda, head of international originals, Latin America, Canada and Australia for Prime Video & Amazon MGM Studios, described “Venganza” as a similar bet for Mexico. The challenge was convincing Amazon that a Mexican production could deliver the scale and action audiences expect from the genre.

	“We believed a Mexican production could tell a story that would resonate globally and demonstrate that great action could come from somewhere other than Hollywood,” she said.
	

	Neither project was an automatic greenlight. Morganti said the teams had to make the case around directors, talent and production capabilities. “You have to keep pushing and show the different elements of why the project could work,” she said.

	That willingness to take risks extends beyond action. Morganti pointed to Spanish-language horror, a genre that was once treated as niche, as another area where Amazon has seen the market expand.

	Success can also open the door to sequels and franchises, although Balmaceda said those opportunities don’t necessarily have to be engineered from the beginning.

	“When you have a success, you naturally look at the audience and the fans around it,” she said. “The important thing is not necessarily to manufacture a franchise, but to recognize when an audience wants more.”

	For creators pitching Amazon, the executives stressed conviction over quantity. Morganti’s advice was straightforward: “You need an original idea and, above all, to really believe in it. Know what you want to tell and why it matters.”

	Balmaceda also emphasized having a clear point of view. “Passion matters,” she said, arguing that creators should know which story they want to tell rather than arrive with a menu of interchangeable concepts.

	Reflecting on Latin America, she noted that its challenge is not necessarily a lack of talent, but a shortage of experience and opportunities to work at scale.

	“Sometimes what’s missing is experience, craft or simply the opportunity to do something at scale,” she said.

	On “Venganza”, a relection of Amazon MGM and El Estudio producer Pablo Cruz‘s push for genre at scale, Amazon brought Bulgarian action specialists to work with the Mexican crew, giving local filmmakers the chance to learn from an experienced international team.

	The discussion comes as Amazon has announced a $2 billion-plus investment in Latin America through 2030, including spending on local content.

	Balmaceda also pushed back on the idea that mass popularity and quality are mutually exclusive. “A hugely popular global title can still involve excellent production, substantial budgets and exceptional talent,” she said.

	Morganti described the current moment for Spanish-language entertainment as a “renaissance,” while saying Amazon’s pipeline remains active. “We’re continuing to develop many projects, and there will be significantly more coming from 2028 onward,” she said, adding that the company is already looking toward 2029 and 2030.
	

	John Hopewell contributed to this article.

schema.headline: Amazon MGM Execs Javiera Balmaceda, Nicole Morganti Talk Big Spanish-Language Action Swings, the Push for Scale at Iberseries & Platino Industria

title: Florence Pugh Credits Tom Holland for ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Role: ‘This All Happened Because of Tom’
description: Florence Pugh appeared on “The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon” Monday night and revealed that fans of her Marvel character, Yelena Belova, reall
body:
Florence Pugh appeared on “The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon” Monday night and revealed that fans of her Marvel character, Yelena Belova, really have Tom Holland to thank for her appearance in “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.”

	“This all happened because of Tom,” said Pugh. “Years ago, when I just started my relationship with Marvel and ‘Black Widow’ came out, my Yelena wasn’t as obviously big as all of the other big superheroes. He, on the red carpet of his previous movie, when someone said, ‘Who do you want to be in the next movie with?… And he said, ‘No, actually, I want to do it with Florence Pugh, who plays Yelena.’ So because of that, fans were then so excited about the idea of it.”
	

	Pugh has played the character of Yelena since 2021 when she appeared in “Black Widow,” and has since reprised the role for 2025’s “Thunderbolts*” and 2026’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.” Within the MCU, Yelena is known as an assassin and the successor to the Black Widow title.


	“Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” which premiered on July 31, has grossed $2.49 billion at the domestic box office, making it the third highest-grossing movie of all time. It ranks behind 2009’s “Avatar” ($2.92 billion) and 2019’s “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.88 billion). “Well done, Spidey!” said Pugh of the accomplishment.

	Scheduled to release in theaters on Dec. 18, Pugh is also set to start as Princess Irulan Corrino once again in “Dune: Part Three” from director Denis Villeneuve. That same day, theatergoers will once again get to see her reprise her role as Yelena in the highly anticipated “Avengers: Doomsday,” the Anthony and Joe Russo-directed follow-up to 2019’s “Avengers: Endgame.”
	

	Watch the full segment here.

                          Wife Files for Divorce

                            6:30 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            "Alaskan Bush People" star Gabriel Brown's wife, Raquell Brown, has filed for divorce after seven years of marriage.
      
    
            Raquell filed the paperwork September 22, claiming their marriage is "irretrievably broken," according to court docs obtained by Us Weekly.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            TMZ broke the story in July the couple had separated after seven years of marriage.
      

            According to court docs, Raquell and Gabe have been living in separate homes since April. Raquell currently resides in Minnesota, while Gabe lives in Washington. They share three children.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Raquell says the couple has no real property, but she's asking the court to fairly divide their personal belongings and assign each of them responsibility for debts incurred after their separation.
      
    
            She's also reserving the right to seek temporary and permanent spousal support, and wants Gabe to cover her attorney fees and other divorce related costs.
      
    
            In addition, Raquell is seeking child support, medical support and contributions toward their children’s daycare, long-distance transportation and education expenses including future college or vocational school costs.
      
    
            Raquell is also asking the court to approve her proposed parenting plan.

title: Accused Cornell Student Blocked on A.I. Platform Months Before Alleged Assault
description:
Accused Cornell Frat Bro
                          A.I. Company Blocked Him
body:
Accused Cornell Frat Bro
                          A.I. Company Blocked Him
                          But Prior to Alleged Assault
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Matthew Ingalls, one of the Cornell students accused of sexually assaulting a classmate, was not fired from DataAnnotation over the case ... but the A.I. company says it did block him from its platform months before the alleged incident occurred.
      
    
            A DataAnnotation spokesperson tells TMZ ... "Jane Doe’s allegations of assault are horrifying. While this individual had signed up on our platform, we blocked him in May 2024. He has had no access to our platform or our company at any point since then."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            DataAnnotation is responding after social posts claiming it had canned Ingalls in the wake of Jane Doe's lawsuit accusing 7 Chi Phi fraternity brothers of gang raping her in October 2024.
      

            We're told Ingalls was an "independent contractor, never an employee" at DataAnnotation. The spokesperson tells us he was blocked in May 2024 ... 5 months prior to the alleged sexual assault of Jane Doe.
      
    
            The company's statement comes as the allegations against the former Cornell students gets renewed attention -- from the public and prosecutors.
      
    
            Jane Doe's lawsuit alleges she was drugged and sexually assaulted at the Chi Phi fraternity house at Cornell.
      
    
            Although she reported the incident to cops back in 2024, prosecutors did not charge anyone with a crime. The Tompkins County District Attorney's Office said it did not have enough evidence back then, but now it's reopening the investigation and plans to present the case to a grand jury.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            All of this is fueling a wave of new social posts doxxing the men's employers and claiming some had been fired after the allegations resurfaced. DataAnnotation is clarifying that is not the case with them.
      
    
            TMZ broke the story ... one of the accused men, Diego Sarabia, did lose his job with Wells Fargo amid the lawsuit and new investigation.
